description: This is a team to build a project for Nasa space app challenge, useful for agriculture fields through spacial dataset
summary:
FieldsTospace is a web app that uses NASA Earth observation data to monitor the health of a farm field from space. The farmer draws or uploads a field boundary, and the app pulls satellite data (Landsat/HLS for crop health, SMAP for soil moisture, GPM IMERG for rainfall, NASA POWER for weather). It calculates NDVI, soil moisture anomaly, and rainfall deficit, then uses K-Means clustering to split the field into management zones. Each zone is scored as healthy, watch, or stressed, and the farmer sees a color-coded map with plain-language alerts like "Zone 2 needs irrigation within 3 days."
The project targets small farmers who can't afford ground sensors. By directing water only to the zones that need it, FieldsTospace helps save water, cut costs, and catch crop stress early. It's built with Python, earthaccess, Rasterio, GeoPandas, scikit-learn, and Streamlit with Folium.
details: FieldsTospace is a web app that uses NASA Earth observation data to monitor the health of a farm field from space. A farmer draws or uploads a field boundary, and the app pulls Landsat/HLS imagery for crop health (NDVI), SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall, and NASA POWER weather data. It splits the field into management zones using K-Means clustering and scores each zone as healthy, watch, or stressed. The farmer sees a color-coded map and plain-language alerts such as "Zone 2 needs irrigation within 3 days." The benefit is water and cost savings for small farmers who can't afford ground sensors, plus early detection of crop stress. It is built with Python, earthaccess, Rasterio, GeoPandas, scikit-learn, and Streamlit with Folium. It is creative because it turns complex satellite data into simple, low-literacy-friendly alerts. We considered resolution limits, cloud cover, and the need for ground validation.
